No page in refs/dotnet-docs contains "open for extension ... closed for modification" verbatim (grep).

"A non-abstract class derived from an abstract class must include actual implementations of all inherited abstract methods and accessors." (abstract.md:47). CS0534: "'function1' does not implement inherited abstract member 'function2' ... A class is required to implement all the abstract members in the base class, unless the class is also abstract." Tried to confirm with dotnet build in a scratch copy; command was not permitted, so evidence is docs only.

Neither test enumerates subclasses, so a new subclass leaves both unchanged (by inspection; test run not permitted).

"An abstract method is implicitly a virtual method." (abstract.md:53). "When you invoke a virtual method, the runtime checks the type of the object for an overriding member. It calls the overriding member in the most derived class." (virtual.md:28). A caller holding a ShippingFee and calling ForOrder needs no edit. Note: the lesson text goes further than this claim ("one line of new code") — see issue on section 4.

Follows from the definition in claim 1: OCP constrains how a new case is added; editing StandardShipping's own threshold (ShippingFee.cs:12) is changing an existing rule, not adding a case. Stated in the lesson with its condition ("because the rule itself changed").

Tautological given the stated condition: if a caller branches on the concrete class, a new class requires editing that branch. The lesson states it conditionally ("If callers checked which class they had..."), not as an absolute.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and overstated: the lesson asserts same-day must be decided in each of the five `express` returns. That is one possible edit, not a necessity: a single `if (sameDay) return ...;` placed before the existing branches would also work. Both are modifications of a working method (the OCP point stands), but "five edits" and "has to be decided in each of the five" are not true of this code. Same overstatement in section 7 suggested answer, summary line 3, and quiz q5 explanation ("five places a new kind would have to be decided").
issues.quote: Same-day would need another flag, and each of those five lines would need to decide what same-day costs there — five edits inside a method that works today.
issues.fix: S5: "Same-day would need another flag, and it has to go somewhere inside this method, among or ahead of branches that work today. Either way you edit the method, and every return next to the edit must be checked again." S7 answer: "has to be added inside the method, next to the five `express` lines, so you edit working code". Summary 3: "...so a new kind means editing that method and re-checking all of them." q5 explanation.correct: "five places that sit next to any new-kind edit". Add a claim for it.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: "one line of new code" is a specific quantity with no support in the repo — at stage-0 nothing outside the tests creates a ShippingFee, so there is no creation site to count. If the creation site maps a user choice to a class (a switch or if-chain), adding same-day there is an edit to existing code, not purely new code. Claim 6 in the ledger only says "some code still has to create an instance".
issues.quote: One place still has to create the new kind, but that is one line of new code, not an edit inside the rules that already work.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Some code still has to create the new kind, but that code sits outside the fee rules; the rules that already work are not edited." Drop "one line". Keep claim 6 as the ledger entry for it.

issues.text: After being told OCP means not editing existing code, I read that some code still has to create the new kind. I cannot tell whether that creating code already exists (and so gets edited) or is new, nor why editing it would be fine under OCP. 'Sits outside the fee rules' reads like an escape hatch without the reason.
issues.quote: Some code still has to create the new kind, but that code sits outside the fee rules; the rules that already work are not edited.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this one saying plainly: that creating code may need a small edit, and OCP here is about keeping the fee rules and their callers closed, not every line in the program.

issues.text: The situation says both places 'work out a shipping fee', so I expected the same rules. Comparing the code blocks, `Smells.ShippingVnd` depends on city and weight (45000/90000 outside two cities) while `StandardShipping`/`ExpressShipping` ignore city. I stopped to wonder whether the class version is a rewrite of the flag version or a different, simpler rule set.
issues.quote: The samples project already works out a shipping fee in two places
issues.fix: Add half a sentence in section 2 or 5 saying the two versions do not compute exactly the same rules; they are compared only for where a new kind would go.

issues.text: q2 explanation for option d mentions 'modules', a word the lesson never uses; it made me wonder if OCP covers something beyond classes that I missed.
issues.quote: OCP is usually applied to classes and modules — in the lesson, to the shipping classes.
issues.fix: Replace with: "OCP is not limited to methods; in the lesson it is applied to the shipping classes."

issues.text: q5 and q3 repeat the Try-it steps and their Expected result almost word for word ('five', 'none; you add one new class'), so they test recall of section 7 rather than understanding. Acceptable, but low value.
issues.quote: Expected result: step 1 gives five — every `return` except the last one, `return 0;`. Step 2 gives none
issues.fix: Optionally change q5 to ask which of the six returns would sit next to a same-day edit placed at the top of the method, so it is not a copy of the Try-it answer.
